summary: Susan L. Huntington works in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1969–1972) and spent her career at Ohio State University as Professor (~1971–2000) and later Distinguished University Professor, Emerita.
Susan Meinheit is a scholar in the field of Tibetology. Her career includes posts at the Library of Congress, attested in 1998 and 2007.

Sinologist and historian Susan Naquin studied at Stanford (BA ~1962–1966) and Yale (MA ~1966–1968, PhD ~1968–1974). She served as assistant professor of history at the University of Pennsylvania (1977–1993) and as professor at Princeton University (1993–2013).

Susan Neiman is a philosopher who studied at Harvard (PhD ~1979–1986) and the Free University of Berlin (1982–1988). She held professorships at Yale (1989–1996) and Tel Aviv University (1996–2000), becoming Director of the Einstein Forum in 2000.
Susan Niditch is a scholar in religious studies. She held a post in the religion department at Amherst College around 1978.

Susan Whitfield specializes in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology. After completing her PhD at SOAS in 1995, she directed the International Dunhuang Project at the British Library (1993–2017) and became Professor at the University of East Anglia.

Susannah Deane works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at Bangor, Bristol, and Cardiff (PhD 2010–2015). Her academic posts include a British Academy Postdoctoral Fellowship at Bristol (2017–2021) and a research bid-writing post at UWE (2023).

Susanne Hoeber Rudolph worked in Indology and political science. She studied at Sarah Lawrence, Radcliffe, and Harvard (PhD ~1953–1955), taught at Harvard (~1954–1963) and the University of Chicago (from 1964), and was president of the APSA (2003–2004).
Susanne Kerekes is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Pennsylvania and held a post at Trinity College, Hartford.

Susanne Mrozik is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned an MTS at Harvard, supervised by Charles Hallisey. She held academic posts at Western Michigan University (attested 2002) and Mount Holyoke College (attested 2009).

Sushanta Sen is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Visva-Bharati University, where he became a lecturer in 1986, and later served as Lecturer in Indian Religions at the University of Birmingham.

Indologist Sushil Kumar De studied at Presidency, Calcutta, SOAS (DLitt ~1919–1921), and Bonn. He taught English at Presidency and Calcutta, served as Professor of Sanskrit at Dhaka (~1923–1947), and led the Bengali department at Jadavpur in 1947.

Susmita Basu Majumdar is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Lady Brabourne College (~1990–1993) and the University of Calcutta (~1993–1998), where she later held a post around 1999.

Susumu Kajiura works in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He held a post as an assistant at Kyoto University in 1999 and served as head of humanities research at Gangoji Institute for Research on Cultural Property (attested 2001).

Susumu Otake is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at the University of Tsukuba under Makio Takemura. He served as a lecturer at Kyoto University (2008), Hanazono University (2008–2013), and Bukkyo University (2012–2013).

Susumu Shimazono specializes in religious studies and Japanology. Educated at the University of Tokyo and UC Berkeley, he was a professor at the University of Tokyo (1995–2013), later holding posts at Sophia University (~2012–2019) and other institutions.

Susumu Winston Nakamura worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Japanology. He earned his MA at the University of California, Berkeley under Ferdinand Lessing (~1937–1941) and served as a lecturer at UC Berkeley and the University of Colorado Boulder (~1942–1946).

Susumu Yamaguchi was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who studied at Otani, Paris, and Kyoto. He was a professor at Otani University (1934–1964) and Kyoto Sangyo University (1964), and directed the Shinshu Otani-ha Research Institute.

Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at London, Pennsylvania, and Toronto. He founded the Nalanda College of Buddhist Studies, serving as president (~1999), and held posts at Ontario Tech University and the University of Toronto.

Suzanne Karpelès was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at INALCO and EPHE under Lévi, Foucher, and Finot. She served at the EFEO, curated the National Library of Cambodia, and founded and directed the Buddhist Institute (1930).
